claims.statement: Poland had 1,636,673 RES micro-installations at the end of 2025, 99.9% of them PV, creating a large installed base rather than only a new-installation market.
URE's 2025 dispute report describes voltage-driven PV shutdowns, confusing net-billing, and cases where misconfigured inverters or heat pumps can raise electricity use.
A meaningful share of these cases can probably be triaged remotely before dispatch, but the fixable share and achievable customer acquisition cost are not yet established.

contrary_evidence: Some shutdowns originate in DSO voltage conditions and cannot be remedied economically at the customer's site.
Inverter vendors and active installers already provide monitoring portals, while residential service tickets may be too small to support paid acquisition.
Complaint evidence demonstrates pain, not the number of owners willing to pay an independent diagnostic fee.

economics.acquisition_route: Acquire high-intent searches around named inverter errors and net-billing disputes, then embed the same structured intake in warranty-claim and service-ticket flows so an insurer or installer can issue a diagnostic link before authorizing a truck roll. The family installation company is a bounded validation pool, not the scale channel.
economics.founder_time: Part-time validation hypothesis; delivery burden remains untested.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A repeatable diagnostic decision tree by inverter, meter, tariff, and DSO; automated document parsers; and a service network measured on first-time-fix and response time reduce diagnosis cost and avoid unnecessary visits. The defensible unit is the integrated resolution workflow and service performance, not a pile of telemetry.
fingerprint.customer: Polish residential prosumers and micro-SMEs with rooftop PV whose original installer is unavailable, whose inverter repeatedly trips, or whose bill no longer matches expected generation; the scalable buyer can also be an insurer, energy retailer, or service firm buying the desk white-label.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Acquire high-intent searches around named inverter errors and net-billing disputes, then embed the same structured intake in warranty-claim and service-ticket flows so an insurer or installer can issue a diagnostic link before authorizing a truck roll. The family installation company is a bounded validation pool, not the scale channel.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Productized intake parses bills, meter exports, inverter logs, installation documents, and interval data into a cause-ranked report. A managed desk then orders only the necessary certified electrician visit, inverter reconfiguration, monitoring retrofit, or repower. Revenue comes from audit fees, annual monitoring, and disclosed coordination margin, while regulated electrical work remains with qualified contractors.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The asset owner pays for a remote bill-and-telemetry audit before dispatch and for a fixed-scope remediation package after accepting the diagnosis; portfolio partners can instead pay per resolved case plus an annual monitoring fee.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A bill spike, inverter alarm, over-voltage shutdown, warranty dispute, or proposed repower creates an urgent need to separate configuration, metering, equipment, consumption, and grid causes before paying for a site visit.

founder_fit: Strong fit with data analysis, anomaly detection, AI-assisted document parsing, and the founder's Polish energy context.
Can start part-time and asset-light with remote audits, using the parents' installation business only for early workflow access and safe contractor validation.
Avoids camera-led marketing and can evolve from a productized service into monitoring and case-management software.
risks: Evidence of a workflow, transition, or loss does not yet establish recurring willingness to pay.
The proposed distribution and compounding mechanisms remain hypotheses pending buyer evidence.

title: PV Rescue Desk for Silent Underperformance
uncertainties: Share of cases attributable to configuration, failed components, metering, changed load, or grid conditions.
Customer permission and practical access to interval-meter and multi-brand inverter data.
Contribution margin after support time, acquisition, and certified field dispatch.
Pricing, buyer authority, and acquisition economics remain unvalidated at discovery.

First validation test: Within 30 days, recruit 40 installations across at least three inverter brands, charge before analysis on at least 15, issue diagnoses without a visit, and compare each diagnosis with a blinded electrician inspection. Continue only if at least half of paid cases yield an actionable finding and the remote gross margin is positive before remediation revenue.
